haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors go only through Redis (cursors entries and cursor:doc pub/sub). The document service and Postgres are not changed and cursors never reach them.
haiku-low.q2: At most one update per 50 ms per client. The node silently drops an update accepted less than 50 ms earlier. The browser keeps only the latest position and sends it when the window ends.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the cursor until that revision is applied. A newer seq from the same connection replaces the held cursor. It is drawn when applied, if its seq is still above the last shown.
haiku-low.q4: It moves the position with transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev). If that throws HistoryGone (older than the editor's kept 500 revisions), the cursor is dropped until the next update from that connection.
haiku-low.q5: Each tab has its own connId and caret, so two tabs may show two carets; one-caret policy is undecided. The user stays listed until their last connection leaves or expires.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, others see the leave within 2 s. After the user's node dies, removal comes at most 40 s after the crash, within the 45 s limit.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis, per document: presence, leases, cursors (each keyed by connId) and presence_ver. Each connection's heartbeat every 10 s moves its lease 30 s ahead and sets keys to expire in 120 s.
haiku-low.q8: A surviving node's sweep (every 10 s, Lua, Redis TIME) removes expired leases and their presence and cursor entries. If it was the user's last connection, it publishes leave on presence:doc, which nodes forward to their browsers.
haiku-low.q9: The sender's node publishes the accepted cursor to cursor:doc in Redis; every subscribed node forwards it to its browsers, including the other node. The same-node path is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: The node subscribes to presence:doc and cursor:doc before the snapshot and forwards events only after it. Browsers skip events at or below the snapshot version and request a new snapshot on a version gap.
haiku-low.q11: Every snapshot is followed by hello. Every browser in the document answers hello by sending its current cursor, rev and position, even when the user is idle.
haiku-low.q12: It drops any cursor whose seq is not above the last seq shown for that connId. A held cursor is replaced only by a newer seq from the same connection, so older positions are never drawn after newer ones.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors are never stored durably and never reach the edit path, document service, Postgres or load balancer. They live only in Redis (cursors key) and pub/sub.
sonnet.q2: At most one cursor update per 50 ms per connection. The browser keeps only the latest position in that window and sends it when the window ends. The node drops silently any update arriving less than 50 ms after the last accepted one, and the browser never learns of the drop.
sonnet.q3: It holds the cursor. A newer seq from the same connId replaces the held one. It draws the cursor when that rev is applied, if its seq is still above the last one shown.
sonnet.q4: It moves pos with transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev) and draws it. If transformPosition throws HistoryGone (rev older than the last 500 revisions kept), it drops the cursor until the next update from that connection.
sonnet.q5: Each tab has its own connId, so carets are keyed by connection and two tabs may show two carets (undecided). The user is listed once: join is published only for the first presence entry. The user disappears (leave published) only when the last connection is gone. On a clean close of the last tab others see it within 2 s. Crash or stall removal takes up to 40 s.
sonnet.q6: After a clean tab close, within 2 s. After a node dies, at most 40 s (30 s lease plus the 10 s sweep), within the 45 s limit.
sonnet.q7: In Redis, with four keys per document (presence, leases, cursors, presence_ver), at per-connection (connId) granularity. Each connection's heartbeat every 10 s moves its lease 30 s ahead and sets key expiry to 120 s.
sonnet.q8: Its leases stop being refreshed and expire. The Lua sweep on a surviving node, running every 10 s, removes the expired connIds' presence and cursor entries. If it was the user's last connection, that script raises presence_ver and publishes leave on presence:doc. Subscribed nodes then forward the leave to their browsers. If no node survives, key expiry clears the keys.
sonnet.q9: The accepting node runs a Lua script that stores the cursor if the connId has a lease, then PUBLISHes it on cursor:doc. Redis pub/sub delivers it to every subscribed node, including the sender's own node, and each node forwards it to its browsers. NOT STATED whether the sender's own node uses a different path.
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to presence:doc and cursor:doc before joining. It reads presence, cursors and presence_ver in one atomic read and sends a snapshot. It forwards events only after the snapshot. The browser ignores presence events with version at or below the snapshot's, applies the rest in order, and asks for a new snapshot if a version number is skipped. Cursors go through the same rules. Every snapshot is followed by hello.
sonnet.q11: After the snapshot, the joining node publishes hello. Every browser in the document answers with its current rev and position, even if idle. Stored cursors from the snapshot also go through the receiving rules.
sonnet.q12: Rule b: it drops a cursor whose seq is not above the last seq shown for that connId. A held cursor is replaced by a newer seq, so an older one is never drawn after a newer one. A reconnect gets a new connId and counter, so an old seq never blocks it.
